Windows chat now includes a checksum-verified Vulkan GPU runtime alongside the CPU fallback. The desktop launcher no longer forces the CPU executable. Uncloud selects the GPU backend when it reports a usable device; an explicit custom runtime still takes precedence. Graphics-driver support is required.

Compatible native GGUF runtimes now fit context and offload placement using llama.cpp’s actual model/cache memory accounting. The displayed window comes from the running backend, instead of being capped again by Uncloud’s dense FP16 estimate. CPU fitting also protects RAM already used by other applications. This does not guarantee a particular context size on every machine.

Custom context Apply reloads the model and displays the allocated window and model maximum. Leaving the field blank and applying resets Auto. Invalid values are rejected before unloading the resident model. Switching text models waits for the old process to exit, including after a forced stop, before starting its replacement.

GGUF replies are bounded to the loaded context instead of allowing unlimited context shifting. Sustained exact reasoning cycles stop with an error and preserve the conversation. Auto thinking, native samplers and tool templates are unchanged; no identity, date or persona instructions are added. Web evidence fitting no longer uses its fitting reserve as an automatic reply ceiling. These safeguards do not guarantee that every model will produce a final answer.

Settings now lists models held across text, image, video, cached transcription, voice and narration modules, with worker/job activity. The text row includes runtime device information and allocated context. Unload all also clears cached voice and narration models. The Guide and installation notes explain the behavior.

Validation: 1,125 backend tests passed (3 skipped), 186 frontend tests passed, and the production frontend build, Python lint and release-resource checks passed. Tests cover allocated context, custom reload/Auto reset, model-stop ordering, runtime selection, resident inventory and repeated-thinking termination without loading model weights. Windows GPU execution and large-context performance still require physical Windows hardware verification.
